chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: Why he entered the hospital: the voucher, Nazarro and a lost Bubbles
summary: Green says the office would not let him go solo, Nazarro was foster parent, he could not find Bubbles to vouch for him, and he entered a hospital where he had to pass the staff.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, anyway, so, basically you decided to go into a hospital for a number of years, because of the lack of your partner and because you weren't working then. That's the basic reason?

Yeah -- well, the basic reason is that I was involved, you see, as I say, I had gotten a voucher, you see. We had work -- we were working, but I mean the real Chuck and Chuckles -- they're the ones that wasn't working, see. You
couldn't take that one and pass off as a number two, you know.
Why didn't you go as a solo?

Well, I mean, it never occurred to me to do as a solo, you know. The office wouldn't have it, you know. See, the office thought maybe I'd get into some kind of bad environment or, you know, get depressed or something, you know. They wasn't having it. They thought --
What did Nat Nazzaro say at that time?
Yeah, well, he was the one, you know. He was the foster parent, you see.

Well, I couldn't find Bubbles. That's who I wanted to be my voucher, you see, at that time. You know, I didn't know where -- that his mother had passed, you know. I hadn't seen any of them. I looked for the sublets, you see, and couldn't find them.

No, no, I wasn't lost. But, I mean, if I put off something, see. If I could get back to the doctors and be reinstated, physically, that was my whole idea, see, of going to the hospital at all. But it was the type of hospital that you couldn't just walk in and get a treatment and walk out. You had to stay there and you have to pass what they call a staff -- pass the staff, see, that's from doctors, specialists, experts, you know.
What do you mean, pass the staff?
Yes. Yes. And you have to be out, you have to be right. When they ask you a question, you have to answer the question correctly, see.
Well, did you feel, then, that you weren't -- you didn't have a good grasp on your life at that particular time?

No, never -- never been that way. I was always a happy person. See, I was full of play -- I was a playful, you know, and I could play with people. Somehow causing them to leave them laughing, as they say, you know.
